title: Petition: Tell Canada to oppose the Mining Code and protect the deep sea from mining.
text:

You're a hero!

Just one more question:

Our work is 100% funded by people like you. We're completely independent from corporate or political donations.

Will you chip in regularly to help protect and preserve the health of the earth?

Share this petition

Every share helps build pressure. Pick a platform below.

Canada-based The Metals Company (TMC) is trying to mine the ocean’s deep sea, an uncharted and pristine territory, by any means necessary. They are aligning with Trump and bypassing the international community to unleash a new era of destructive extraction for profit, at the expense of nature and global cooperation.[1] [2]

The Canadian government must step in now.

For the last decade, the International Seabed Authority (ISA) has worked to develop a set of rules – officially known as the Mining Code – that would legitimize deep sea mining and unlock vast areas of the ocean for exploitation [3].

Last Spring, in a reckless series of harmful executive orders, Trump unilaterally fast-tracked deep sea mining permits, paving the way for wanna-be tech-bro Gerard Barron, CEO of The Metals Company, to bulldoze ahead with their deep sea mining plans – without any global rules in place [1] [4]. This isn’t innovation, it’s looting the ocean floor, and we cannot let it happen.

So far, the newly elected Canadian government has stayed dangerously silent, but now’s the time for Carney and Minister of Foreign Affairs Minister Anand to lead the charge to protect the world’s oceans.

With science warning of irreversible damage from mining the seabed, and rogue behaviour from Trump and Barron, it has become clear that deep sea mining is an industry that the ocean cannot afford, and that it should never see the light of day. [5]

We’re calling on Prime Minister Carney and Minister Anand to:

- Reaffirm Canada's support for a global moratorium on deep sea mining- Oppose a rushed Mining Code that would legalize seabed exploitation- Stand up to Trump and The Metals Company’s corporate greed

The deep sea isn’t up for grabs. Add your name to demand that Canada lock the seabed out of reach for extractive industries.

Despite relentless efforts from industry actors, deep sea mining remains at a standstill. Our movement continues to grow and we are making significant progress, in Canada and around the world. We are hopeful: we can still stop this industry before it starts!

More than 3 million people are opposing the deep sea mining industry with Greenpeace.

More than 40 countries support a moratorium or a precautionary pause on deep sea mining.

More than 5,500 known species have a chance to thrive if deep sea mining never begins in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone.
